thread:
samir.p: Thinking out loud — for the high-throughput inference path (millions of requests/day) we need to re-evaluate envelope design. Question: how aggressive can we be with DEK unwrap caching while still meeting audit & rotation constraints across AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure Key Vault? :thinking:

ben_s: TL;DR: cache unwrapped DEKs in local memory with a short TTL + strict RBAC + audit logging on unwrap and rotation events. But details matter (scope, TTL, rekey).

maria.eng: Agree. Important to separate concerns: DEK lifecycle (short-lived, per-blob or per-session) vs KEK usage (wrap/unwrap via KMS). We should avoid doing KMS calls per inference token.

samir.p: Proposed model: generate DEK per document-upload (or per-session for streaming). Store ciphertext(DEK) in object metadata. At inference time, fetch object, read ciphertext(DEK), consult local unwrap cache keyed by ciphertext hash, otherwise call KMS to unwrap, cache plaintext DEK in memory for X seconds. Thoughts on X?

kelly.security: We need to balance security and ops. For most infra, TTL=60s-300s is reasonable for high-throughput paths. But for sensitive customers, TTL should be 0 or very short. Also require per-unwrap audit event emitted to SIEM even when served from cache? We can't log plaintexts. Log metadata: unwrap_event with key_id, ciphertext_sha256, cache_hit boolean, principal.

ben_s: Exactly. Cache policy suggestion:
```yaml
unwrap_cache:
  ttl_seconds: 120       # default for hosted inference
  max_plaintext_entries: 10000
  max_memory_mb: 512
  per_principal_isolation: true
  log_on_cache_hit: true
```
Note: log_on_cache_hit logs a hash and principal, not the key.

taylor_infra: Implementation notes: use LRU + jittered TTL to avoid stampedes. When TTL expires, background rewrap/refresh can proactively refresh for hot keys. Use consistent hashing by ciphertext hash to shard cache across workers so unwrap rate to KMS is bounded per-key.

maria.eng: Also consider a KMS call budget + exponential backoff per-key and circuit breaker. If KMS rate limit hit, return fallback (lower fidelity model) or fail closed depending on customer tier. We already have routing for region fallback, could reuse.

samir.p: RBAC/Q: who should be allowed to request unwraps? We should restrict to service principals only, and human ops only via vault admin. Suggest policy: KMS allow:Decrypt for `redwood-inference/*` roles; deny for general infra. Add condition on tag: `purpose=unwrap-inference` so audits can filter.

kelly.security: Agree. Also add KMS logging config: enable key usage logs to CloudTrail/CloudAudit/KeyVault logs and ship to central SIEM. Map principal -> team and alert on unusual unwrap volume (anomaly detection).

samir.p: Vulnerability scenario: worker compromised and exfiltrates plaintext DEKs. Mitigations?

ben_s: Short TTL helps — transient plaintext in RAM reduces window. In addition: encrypt DEK in a process-isolated enclave when possible (mTLS between inference process and encryptor). Use mlock to avoid swap. Rotate KEKs and run rewrap for stored DEKs (object-level re-encryption) for worst-case.

maria.eng: Incident playbook sketch:
1) Detect abnormal unwrap rate for a principal -> auto-suspend principal.
2) Identify affected ciphertext hashes -> mark objects needing rewrap.
3) Rotate KEK (create new key in KMS, update KEK alias -> new key id).
4) Background job: re-encrypt DEKs with new KEK for affected objects, mark rewrap completed.
5) Force clients to fetch new DEK ciphertext next read (invalidate caches).
This needs to be runnable in <24h for P1.

kelly.security: Add audit requirements to the playbook: timestamps for step 1-4, runbook owner, communication templates, and SBO contact. Also require post-incident keys rotation verification step.

taylor_infra: Minor ops detail: cache invalidation — we need a global invalidation signal. Publish an invalidation message to our pubsub on KEK rotation and any suspicious principal suspension. Workers should evict by ciphertext hash. Avoid broadcasting plaintext.

samir.p: Example config we can add to deployment flags: 
```json
{"envelope_cache": {"enabled": true, "ttl_seconds": 120, "isolation": "per-tenant", "max_entries": 5000}}
```
And a flag `permit_unwrap_logs=true` that turns on compressed audit-shipping for indexers.

ben_s: For cross-cloud: abstract KMS client behind a keystore plugin. Each plugin should expose UnwrapAsync with built-in retry/backoff and a `cost_estimate` to help autoscaler. Also centralize key aliases so rekeying is uniform.

ops-bot: Deploy scheduled: unwrap-cache rollout in canary tonight at 23:00 UTC. See runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/unwrap-cache-rollout :rocket:

kelly.security: Approve canary but require SIEM filters and rate-anomaly alert configured before broad rollout. Also require docs for customer opt-outs (e.g., require no caching for certain compliance customers).

samir.p: Cool — I'll draft the PR with the config defaults and runbook updates. Thanks all. :lock:
